content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Matrix optimization removes redundant combinations, limits parallel jobs, and preserves coverage for every supported OS/runtime combination. Optimize from measured workflow duration and usage. Remove redundant work, cache only rebuildable dependencies, parallelize independent jobs, and keep retry behavior bounded. items.title: Reducing duplicate matrix combinations
items.text: List the supported combinations explicitly and use `include`/`exclude` or `max-parallel` to control expansion. Keep all required configurations covered and avoid unnecessary duplicate jobs.

items.title: Limiting concurrent jobs
items.text: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.

items.title: Evaluating execution time against cost
items.text: Measure duration, resource/runner consumption, queue time, and failure rate before changing the pipeline. Bound retries, cancel stale work only when safe, and compare the result after one controlled change.

content_blocks.code:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]
        python: ["3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}
      - run: python -m unittest discover -s tests
content_blocks.expected_output: The test job expands into four OS/Python combinations. A real repository must contain a compatible `tests` directory.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Insert this job under `jobs` in a workflow. For production use, review and pin third-party actions to verified immutable references according to your policy.

troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
